Her husband was paralyzed. She finished the Brooklyn Bridge. 🌉 Watch 14 years of building in 25 seconds. ⏱️

Designer John Roebling died before work even started. His son Washington took over, sinking giant caissons into the East River, but "the bends" from the compressed-air work left him partly paralyzed. He watched the work by telescope from his room, and his wife Emily Warren Roebling became the link to the site: relaying orders, doing the calculations and supervising for about 11 years.

In 1883 she was the first to cross. A year later, 21 circus elephants walked over it to prove it was safe.

yt_description:
John A. Roebling was fatally injured in 1869 before construction began (2 Jan 1870). Son Washington Roebling built the compressed-air caissons (Brooklyn 44.5 ft, Manhattan 78.5 ft deep) and was partly paralyzed by caisson disease; he watched by telescope while Emily Warren Roebling relayed, calculated and supervised for ~11 years. Towers 1875–76; first wire 1876; 5,282 wires per main cable; opened 24 May 1883 (Emily first across); 21 elephants crossed on 17 May 1884.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Bridge · https://www.history.com/articles/brooklyn-bridge
